abstract: We prove that the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomially bounded in its input length, resolving a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa, and Jiang. If the defining system has dense binary encoding length $L$, then $O((L+1)^9)$ split rounds suffice to reach the integer hull in arbitrary dimension.
hook: Polynomially many split-cut rounds, at most order (L+1)^9, always reach the integer hull.
summary: The paper proves the split rank of a rational pure-integer polyhedron is polynomial in its encoding length L, with O((L+1)^9) rounds enough in any dimension. This confirms a conjecture of Basu, Conforti, Di Summa and Jiang. The ninth-power bound is likely far from tight, and it is a rank bound, not a faster solver.
title: A Polynomial Bound on Split Rank
